subject: SLA & premium support packaging — follow-up and action items from pricing workshop
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@skyline.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA options — few clarifying questions after the workshop

Ben — thanks again for running that pricing workshop this morning. Helpful framing. A couple of quick clarifying questions so we can take this back to procurement: 

1) You mentioned a staged uptime ladder (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) — can you share the exact SLA credit percent buckets tied to each band (and how they scale with commit)? Our procurement team needs the math so they can model expected credits over a year.

2) On the premium support side, there was a suggestion to package ‘on-call retainer + rapid response’ as a sku. Can you provide an example SKU (what’s included: X hours on-call, Y rapid-response incidents, Z postmortems) and the list price vs. a 1-year committed discount?

3) Is there a regional failover surcharge for cross-region failover (we plan to have primary in us-west and DR in eu-west)? If so, what does that look like for our projected Q4 usage (~$75k/mo run-rate)?

If you can send the above as a short note (or the workbook from the deck), I’ll share with procurement today.

—Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Director of Infrastructure, Skyline AI
phone: (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@skyline.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA options — few clarifying questions after the workshop

Thanks Olivia — great follow-up. I’m looping Stephanie (our Head of Pricing) and will attach the workbook with band math. High-level answers below; workbook has line-item formulas.

1) SLA credit buckets (examples):
- 99.9% (Standard): 5% service credit of monthly committed spend per incident window.
- 99.95% (Enhanced): 10% credit.
- 99.99% (Premium): 25% credit + guaranteed incident review within 72 hours.

Credits scale with commit: for committed annual contracts we reduce the baseline credit by 25% (i.e., committed customers get fewer credits monetized; instead we offer deeper upfront discounts). See sheet 'Credit_vs_Commit' — examples at 12/24/36 month commits.

2) Premium support SKU example (example name: 'RapidAssist-24'):
- Included: 24/7 escalation path, 2 x guaranteed <60min P1 responses per month, 8 hours dedicated on-call retainer per month, 2 incident postmortems/quarter, runbook integration.
- List price: $18,000/month (for our standard price band).
- 1-year commit example: 12% discount on list price; 24-month: 18% discount.

3) Regional failover surcharge: yes — cross-region active/passive failover incurs an inter-region networking & standby capacity surcharge. Typical guideline: 8–12% of committed monthly spend as a failover add-on (sliding based on reserved capacity). For your $75k/mo run-rate that translates to ~$6k–9k/mo depending on redundancy profile. We can model a cheaper option (rolling cold-standby + automated warm-up) that reduces the surcharge to ~4–6%.

I’ve attached the pricing workbook and SKU appendix. Stephanie — can you confirm the discount ladders and whether we can offer a one-time onboarding credit for Skyline given the multi-region ask?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@skyline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA options — few clarifying questions after the workshop

Hi Olivia / Ben — thanks for the summary. Quick notes / confirmations from pricing ops: 

- Discount ladder: we can firm up a table for you. Example (applies to support SKU list price and base inference consumption):
  * No commit: 0%
  * 12-month commit (>= $600k ARR): 8%
  * 24-month commit: 14%
  * 36-month commit: 20%

- SLA credit monetization: for customers who accept committed-discount structure we cap SLA credits at 50% of the nominal credit exposure (that’s how we protect economics while giving procurement cover). 

- Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to one month of the support SKU (effectively waiving the first month) for 12-months+ commitments. For larger commits we can consider an additional professional services credit applied to the first invoice.

- For Skyline specifically (based on Ben's $75k/mo): if they go 24-month commit, recommended offer: 14% off consumption + RapidAssist-24 at 16% off list + first month waived on RapidAssist. Also offer a DR warm-standby option at 5% surcharge instead of the 8–12% full failover surcharge.

I’ll attach a compact 'Offer_summary' page that Ben can send to procurement. Marissa — FYI on margin callouts.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail procurement wanted. A couple follow-ups before I share with the broader team: 

- For the onboarding credit, can we get that as a line-item in the MSA (so it shows on the SOW/invoice) rather than applied as a separate bill credit? Procurement insists on line-item transparency.

- The DR warm-standby option at 5% sounds promising. Can you also add a sentence on RTO expectations for that profile (we're targeting sub-15 min warm-up for core endpoints)?

If you can add those two clarifications to the Offer_summary and re-send, I’ll circulate today and ask for a procurement sync Friday morning.

—Olivia
